# Plan: harness hardening before the distillation work

Cluster plumbing works (`548fde5` submit, `950d74e` toy training). This plan covers
what to add before the distillation work starts.

**"Distillation" here** = training on CoT traces pre-generated by strong models,
i.e. offline SFT. No teacher in the loop, no KL-on-logits. The work is mostly in
the **data pipeline** (§9), not a custom loss.

**Sections are in implementation order.** §1 is done; start at §2.

## Reference repos

| | plan-crl (local) | nano `ctx_scl` | scaling-crl |
|---|---|---|---|
| config | **tyro + mrunner** | Hydra/OmegaConf | tyro |
| submit | mrunner + shim | homegrown `run_exp.py` | hand-written `job.slurm` |
| domain | LLM SFT/RL, math CoT | LLM pretraining, same lab | JAX/brax RL |
| relevance | **highest** — same stack, same problem | cluster + logging patterns | little |

## 1. Label masking bug — DONE

Was `ids["labels"] = ids["input_ids"].copy()` with `padding="max_length"`: pads
never masked to `-100`, so loss was computed on every pad position — on short
TinyStories samples the objective was dominated by "predict EOS forever".

Now masked via `attention_mask`, which is the only reliable signal: verified
`pad_token_id == eos_token_id == 0` on SmolLM2, so masking by token id would
also drop real end-of-sequence targets.

**Left open:** SmolLM2's tokenizer appends no eos, so nothing is EOS-supervised —
the model now learns no stopping behaviour (better than the wrong one). Resolved
for chat data in §9.2; the raw-text path needs a manual append.

## 2. Checkpoints are landing on `$HOME` — DO FIRST

`train_output_dir="out"` is inside the mrunner-copied repo, which lands under
`storage_dir: /home/j321m/coding_distill` — entropy's `$HOME`, the filesystem with
the **file-count quota** that the whole out-of-tree pixi setup exists to avoid.
Move to `$PROJECT_HOME_PATH=/storage_nvme_4/coding_distill` alongside `HF_HOME`
(export `$RUN_OUT` in `clusters.yaml` `prolog_cmd`, default from it).

### Cadence: linear for now

`save_steps` + `save_total_limit`. No callback yet. Grow into
`nano/src/core/trainer.py:149` when needed — `interval_match or step_match`, i.e.
uniform interval **or** an explicit step list, so log-spacing later is a config
list, not new code. Their `_should_save_final_checkpoint` also avoids a duplicate
save at the last step.

Recorded, not doing now:
- log-spaced steps (probably right for a scaling study)
- dense-at-the-ends (`scaling-crl/train.py:1017`)
- weights-only for historical checkpoints — full ckpt is ~3-4x model size;
  optimizer state only needed on the newest. Matters a lot at 7B (§10).

## 3. Structured stdout — in Python, not `export`

Adopt `logging` as in `nano/main.py:29`:

```python
logging.Formatter(fmt=f"[%(levelname)s][host:{platform.node()}]"
                      f"[local_rank:{os.environ.get('LOCAL_RANK')}] %(message)s")
```

`StreamHandler.emit()` flushes per record, so slurm buffering is solved as a side
effect — no `flush=True`, no env var. Host + local_rank in the formatter is what
makes a 4-GPU log readable. Optionally `sys.stdout.reconfigure(line_buffering=True)`
in `main.py` for third-party prints.

MFU: a flush is a `write()` syscall, µs against steps of 10-100ms — under 0.01%
even at `logging_steps=1`. The `.item()` device sync is the real cost and HF pays
it at every logging step anyway. Gate expensive *metrics* (§6), not cheap prints.

Print derived config values at startup.

## 4. tyro + mrunner — SOLVED, copy plan-crl

Both live together via a subprocess shim. mrunner never sees tyro's flags.

`plan-crl/mrunner_run.py` (30 lines) — the whole trick:
- `get_configuration()` -> flat dict
- pops `entry_point` (selects which training script; one shim, many scripts)
- flat dict -> CLI flags: `bool` -> `--flag` / `--no-flag`, `list` -> `--k a b c`,
  else `--k v`
- `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", entry_point] + flags)`

Config keys are **dotted** — `"llm_actor.engine_args.model_id"` -> `--llm_actor.engine_args.model_id`
-> tyro's nested-dataclass syntax. Arbitrarily nested typed config, still flat for
mrunner sweeps.

Also copy:
- `plan-crl/mrunner_run_local.py` — runs a spec locally through the same shim, no
  code upload, `--job-index N` for one job of a grid. Same code path local and
  remote; replaces our `pixi run debug`.
- `.mrunnerignore` file instead of the inline `EXCLUDE` list in `configs/toy.py`.
- `create_experiments_helper(base_config=..., params_grid=...)` instead of
  hand-built `Experiment`.
- Field docstrings in the dataclasses — tyro renders them in `--help`
  (`plan-crl/plan_crl/config/args.py`, 620 lines, good model).

Add `tyro` to `pixi.toml`. Must switch cleanly between the debug model and the
7B student (§10).

**Open:** keep `nesting_prefixes` or move to dotted keys? Dotted is what makes
tyro nesting work — probably drop the prefix scheme.

## 6. wandb

- Entity `ideas_cv`.
- Log full resolved config. **§4 before §6.**
- **Offline vs online is cluster-dependent** — nano runs online on entropy;
  plan-crl uses `wandb_osh.TriggerWandbSyncHook` offline. Check entropy egress,
  then pick. Support both.
- `_init_wandb_with_retry` — 300s timeout, 3 attempts, backoff on `CommError`
  (`nano/src/core/metric_loggers.py:19`).
- **Rank-0 guard** (`WandbLogger(should_log=...)`). We're on `gpu:4` — mandatory.
- **Dual x-axis**: `define_metric("steps/*", step_metric="step")` +
  `("tokens/*", step_metric="token_count")`. Retrofitting means re-running.
- `MetricLogger` ABC with `wandb`/`stdout`/`dummy` backends — local runs never
  touch wandb.
- `_pending` dict + `flush()` — one `run.log()` per step.
- `heavy_metrics_calculation_interval` — gate expensive metrics only.
- **Secrets**: forward `WANDB_API_KEY`/`HF_TOKEN` via `Experiment(env=...)`, never
  hardcoded. nano substitutes placeholders at submit time
  (`resolver/__init__.py`, `run_exp.py:411`).

**Open:** `report_to="wandb"` vs own `wandb.init` + callback. Leaning: init
ourselves, let HF attach.

## 8. Train-loss + metric logging in the trainer

Nothing is logged today. Copy `nano/src/core/trainer.py:386`:

- Frozen `LossMetrics` dataclass: `total_loss` (backprop) vs `reported_loss`
  (plain CE). The seam where an auxiliary term slots in later.
- Per step: `train/loss`, `train/lr` (from `scheduler.get_last_lr()[0]`, not
  config — catches scheduler bugs), `train/grad_norm`.
- `AveMetric(100, "100/train/loss")` — tail-averaged window, emitted once per 100
  steps. `AveDiffMetric` gives step time the same way.
- `processed_tokens += batch.numel() * WORLD_SIZE` -> `set_tokens()` for §6's
  token axis.

HF's Trainer gives loss/lr/grad_norm free via `report_to`. Not free: token axis,
tail-averaged windows, total-vs-reported split. Subclass `Trainer`, override
`compute_loss`, add a callback.

## 9. CoT data pipeline — the actual work

**Dataset: `open-r1/codeforces-cots`** (R1 traces on Codeforces problems). 11
configs; start `solutions_decontaminated` (40.7k ex, 7.7GB) or
`solutions_py_decontaminated` (8.1k, Python) for bring-up.

Measured (300-row sample + dataset-server statistics):

| | prompt | completion | total |
|---|---|---|---|
| p50 | 691 | 11,575 | **12,237** |
| p90 | 1,025 | 21,537 | 22,349 |
| max | 1,878 | 24,000 | 25,878 |

Copy plan-crl's shape wholesale rather than patching the current one:
- `scripts/tokenize_dataset.py:57` — tokenize ragged, **no padding, no
  truncation**; `labels = [-100] * prompt_len + input_ids[prompt_len:]`
- `sft_train_fast.py:468` `collate` — dynamic pad, `pad_sequence(labels,
  padding_value=-100)`, `attention_mask` built from true lengths (not recovered
  from ids)
- their truncation is **left**-sided (`x["input_ids"][-max_seq_length:]`, keeping
  the tail). Fits their agentic rollouts; **does not transfer here** — see 4.

1. **Prompt masking** — `-100` on prompt tokens. **Low-stakes** for this dataset:
   prompt is p50 691 tokens against a p50 11.6k completion, so masking moves ~5%
   of the loss. Do it (`messages[:1]` is the prompt) and stop deliberating.
2. **Chat templating** — codeforces-cots ships `messages` = `[user, assistant]`,
   2 turns, so `apply_chat_template(..., add_generation_prompt=False)` gives both
   the prompt boundary and the end-of-turn token. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct has a
   template; eos is `<|im_end|>` and a manual append on top would be a bug.
   SmolLM2-135M (base, debug only) has `chat_template = None` — the manual append
   is for that path only, and must be conditional on the model.
3. **Padding** — dynamic, mandatory. Lengths run 502 → 25.9k;
   `padding="max_length"` would waste roughly half the compute. Packing is not
   worth it at these lengths — samples already fill a batch row.
4. **Truncation — resolved by the model choice.** Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct's
   context is **32768**, and 32k holds 100% of samples. No length-based dropping,
   no truncation policy. Set `max_length=32768` and **assert rather than
   truncate** — a sample that doesn't fit is a bug to look at, not something to
   silently cut.
   - Still drop `finish_reason == "length"`: traces R1 itself cut off (4.2%,
     1716/40665). Free flag, no heuristic.
   - Left-truncating would be wrong here — the problem statement is at the front,
     so cutting the head leaves the model reasoning about an unseen problem.
   - `max_length=512` in `configs/toy.py` is debug-only; it covers ~0% of real
     samples.

## 10. Training at 7B / 32k — what the model choice costs

The dataset authors used **`Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct`** as the student.
32768 context, chat template present, `pad_token` (`<|endoftext|>`) is a
*different* id from `eos_token` (`<|im_end|>`) — the pad==eos hazard of §1 goes
away, though masking off `attention_mask` stays correct and model-agnostic.

Nothing in the current `TrainingArguments` supports this scale. Needed:

- **Sharding.** Persistent state ≈ 15GB weights + 15GB grads + ~91GB AdamW fp32
  (m, v, master) ≈ 122GB against 4×80GB. Fits only sharded — FSDP full-shard or
  DeepSpeed ZeRO-3. Add an `accelerate` config; pick one.
- **Gradient checkpointing** — non-negotiable at 32k.
- **flash-attention-2** — 32k attention is otherwise quadratic in memory.
- `per_device_train_batch_size=1` + gradient accumulation for the effective batch.
- Add `flash-attn`, `accelerate`, and (if chosen) `deepspeed` to `pixi.toml`.

Scale sanity check: 40.7k samples × ~12.2k tok ≈ **500M tokens/epoch**. Order
10h/epoch on 4×H100 — inside entropy's 2-day limit, but no longer a loop you
iterate on. Keep SmolLM2-135M as the debug model.

Worth cribbing: open-r1 published recipes for this dataset — check their
hyperparameters and sharding config before guessing.

## 11. Eval via lm-eval-harness

`src/eval.py`. nano already integrates it (`src/core/eval.py`).

Our models are HF, so `lm_eval.models.huggingface.HFLM` works directly — skip
nano's 246-line `NanoLM(LM)` wrapper and `_SimpleAccelerator` shim.

Copy: `downstream_eval_interval: 0  # 0 = disabled`; evaluator **owns its cadence**
(`eval_interval`/`final_eval` live on it, Trainer reads them off — `trainer.py:60`);
a `limit:` field so smoke tests take seconds.

**Open:**
- In-loop vs post-hoc. nano does in-loop. Code evals need generation of ~12k-token
  traces and are slow -> leaning post-hoc over checkpoints as separate jobs, plus
  cheap in-loop held-out CE for a live signal.
- Task set. LiveCodeBench / Codeforces-style pass@k is the target; held-out
  perplexity for bring-up.
- Add `lm-eval` to `pixi.toml`.

## Not adopting

- **Online distillation** — nano's `TrainerDistillation` does teacher forwards
  in-loop with KL+temperature. Wrong setup for us; its `LossMetrics`/`log_metrics`
  shape is still the model for §8.
- **Visualization** — no env to roll out.
- **Giant f-string `run_name`** — wandb config holds hparams; short name + timestamp.
- **`int`-as-`bool` flags** (`scaling-crl`'s `use_relu: int = 0`) — §4 gives real bools.
- **Hand-patching `.venv`** (scaling-crl README's brax fix) — vendor or fork.
- **nano's `run_exp.py` git-cemetery submission** — 442 lines replacing what
  mrunner does for us.
